llm.summary: The skill is not malicious, but it asks for broad read/write/command execution authority while its game-asset purpose and operating boundaries are too loosely defined.

dimensions.detail: The manifest declares read, write, and exec tools. Write access can fit asset creation, but shell execution plus broad development/deployment routing is high-impact and not narrowly scoped in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The artifact contains only a SKILL.md file with metadata and instructions; no installer scripts, bundled executables, hidden files, or automatic setup behavior were present.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions are vague: they ask the user to invoke the skill and provide inputs, but do not define concrete tool limits, approval points, safe command boundaries, or prohibited actions.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No actual persistence mechanism was implemented in the inspected file, though the text advertises paid workflow features such as scheduled triggers and event-driven execution. It also gives only generic API key handling guidance without a concrete integration.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifact presents itself as AI game asset generation, but the activation text also covers generic code generation, programming help, debugging, testing, development, and deployment, which is broader than the named asset-generation purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with a broadly scoped game-development assistant that can read files, write files, and run commands. Prefer using it in a sandboxed project folder, and require explicit confirmation before any command execution, deployment action, or modification outside generated game assets.
llm.findings:
[SDI-1] unexpected: Confirmed: the description expands from game asset generation into general coding, debugging, testing, and deployment, creating scope ambiguity.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Confirmed as a Review concern: exec is declared, but the skill does not provide concrete command restrictions or a narrow operational need tied to asset generation.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Confirmed: the activation language is broad enough to route unrelated software engineering tasks into this skill despite write and exec authority.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Confirmed: the invocation section lacks boundaries, approval requirements, and explicit limits on filesystem writes or command execution.
